text:
marta gomez: heads-up — onboarding 'llama-x-8k' HF export to Redwood. after running the quant pipeline, several convo tests started failing.
josh li: can you paste the failure pattern?
marta gomez: short repro: conversation output truncates and occasionally injects <pad> in the middle of replies. raw decode shows PAD token used where BOS/EOS expected.
marta gomez: ran quick inspect:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/llama-x-8k')
print(t.special_tokens_map)
print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<bos>','<eos>','<pad>','<unk>']))
```
josh li: what did it print?
marta gomez: it printed: {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token":"<pad>"} and ids [1, 2, 1, 0] — pad and bos share id 1.
samir patel: that's a red flag. I think the tokenizer merge step that consumes added_tokens.json is reindexing tokens and not preserving special_tokens_map ids during quant step.
aaron_k: did the float32 (non-quant) import keep IDs stable?
marta gomez: yes, float32 import used [0,2,3,1] mapping (pad=0,bos=2,eos=3,unk=1). issue appears only after quantization path because we run token merge inside the quant toolchain which enumerates added_tokens and rewrites tokenizer.json.
token-checker-bot: /token-scan result: special token ID collisions found — pad==bos (id=1). Recommendation: fail import on collision.
josh li: root cause: our quantizer calls merge_added_tokens(tokenizer, added_tokens) which does something like `for i, tok in enumerate(added_tokens): tokenizer.add_tokens(tok)` without preserving original special token ids. That will reuse lower ids if added_tokens includes a token mapping.
samir patel: quick mitigation: change merge to reserve indexes for special tokens and remap only free ids. Also persist original special_tokens_map in config.json and reapply after any token additions.
aaron_k: we also saw perf regressions in llm-bench: +9% perplexity on conv dataset and doubled rerank error rate. Probably downstream because decodes are semantically shifted when BOS/EOS wrong.
marta gomez: I pushed a local fix: tools/remap_specials.py that enforces mapping and rewrites tokenizer artifact. Example usage:
```bash
python tools/remap_specials.py --in out/tokenizer.json --mapping '{"pad":0,"bos":1,"eos":2}' --out out/fixed_tokenizer.json
```
marta gomez: after remap and reimporting quant artifact, conv QA moved back in line (streaming breaks dropped from ~6% -> 0.8%).
josh li: can you add a unit test that permutes added_tokens order and ensures special token IDs are preserved? this caught us because an added_token landed at id 1.
samir patel: yes. also add an audit step to token-import CI that runs: decode(encode("<bos>hello<eos>")) == "<bos>hello<eos>" and a small embedding similarity check for a few anchor prompts.
qa-dog: QA smoke after the remap: streaming break rate 0.8%, sample-level rouge delta within expected noise. full regression job queued.
marta gomez: filing a proper patch to quant tool to stop re-running merges and to reuse the saved tokenizer artifact. will also add import-time collision detection and fail fast.
josh li: creating INF-4321 with repro, sample tokenizer.json, and the remap script. assigning to eng-ml/tokenization and tagging @samir patel for review.
marta gomez: thanks everyone. cc @aaron_k @samir patel :thumbsup:
